02 — CASE STUDIES

Process, before the polish

Earlier UX work — from a hospital app for elderly patients to a capstone time-management app — built through research, testing and iteration.

CASE 01

TUH for All

Redesign · Thammasat University Hospital patient app

The hospital's own app served patients who are mostly senior citizens managing presbyopia and myopia — but its dense menus and small tap targets worked against them. I restructured the information architecture around one priority per screen, enlarged touch targets, and made the patient's own identity (name, HN number, photo) visible immediately after login to reduce anxiety.

  • TargetSenior citizens, majority of TUH's patients
  • MethodUsability testing + interviews, chosen over surveys for direct feedback from elderly users
  • PrinciplesLarger type, high-contrast color, one action per screen, always-visible identity & easy return-to-home
CASE 02

ZenTime

Capstone · Minimalist time-management app · React Native

Built for Pang, a 32-year-old office worker whose old to-do app had "more features than necessary" — this one strips time management down to what's essential. I designed against the Eisenhower matrix for prioritization and a 60-30-10 monochromatic palette in warm neutrals, then built it in React Native with an offline SQLite store.

  • ResearchPersona & pain-point interviews; tested with 6 users, ages 19–33
  • StackReact Native, SQLite (offline-first), Figma prototyping
  • FindingUsers created & reviewed tasks smoothly; main friction was deleting items & unclear icons — fixed in the next iteration
CASE 03

Chicken Ready (ฟาร์มไก่พร้อม)

Field research · Farm-management app for small poultry farmers

On-site visits with chicken farmers surfaced a specific problem: inconsistent record-keeping was quietly eating into already-thin margins. I designed a guided, step-by-step flow for logging flock size, feed costs and expenses — built to be usable by owners with little app experience, not just easy for me to specify.

  • UsersSmall-scale chicken farmers, first-time app users
  • GoalClear income/expense tracking & hygiene guidance in one place
  • ApproachWizard-style forms over dashboards — one number at a time, not a spreadsheet

04 — ABOUT

Computer science, with a design habit

I'm a UX/UI designer and Computer Science graduate from Thammasat University, seven months into my first design role. My work sits where human-computer interaction meets frontend build — I care as much about whether a 70-year-old patient can find the "home" button as I do about whether the grid actually holds up in the browser.

Before design, I spent time on the other side of "user experience" entirely — as a choreographer and assistant stylist for GMM TV productions, and staffing concerts and book fairs across Bangkok. Directing where a body moves on stage isn't so different from directing where an eye moves on a screen; both are about rhythm, and about never making someone think twice.

Right now I'm redesigning customer-facing websites for sports & fitness retail brands, while keeping one foot in research-driven case work — personas, usability testing, and design systems I can hand off, not just hand-wave.
